clue.text: Weed bed in front of lawn

indicators.note: puts the first piece ahead of the second in the answer

parts.note: a couch is a piece of furniture to lie on, a bed of sorts
a lawn is an expanse of grass

explanation.surface: A gardener spots a weed growing between the flower bed and the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Couch grass is a creeping perennial plant that gardeners treat as a pest, so it is a classic weed.

clue.text: 12 ac changed to Iberian city

indicators.note: the letters of the two pieces are altered into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 12 across is POOR, used here as fodder

explanation.surface: An instruction to alter an earlier answer so it names a city in Spain or Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges the letters of POOR (12 across) together with TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto is the English name for Porto, the Portuguese city famous for port wine, on the Iberian peninsula.

clue.text: It's hard to discard a club

parts.note: to cast off is to throw away or discard
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A golfer complains it is difficult to give up one of their clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast iron is a brittle, very hard alloy, and 'cast-iron' also means unbreakable.

clue.text: Order in school

explanation.surface: A religious order runs a school.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greyfriars are Franciscan friars, a religious order named for their grey habits; Greyfriars is also the fictional boarding school of Billy Bunter stories.

clue.text: Pupil's usual mistake about centre of alphabet

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the middle letters of the alphabet
a mistake garbles the word usual, so its letters are reordered

parts.note: M and N are the 13th and 14th of the 26 letters, the very middle of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A schoolchild commonly gets wrong the letters in the middle of the alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' looks like the schoolchild of the surface, but here means a former student; the letters MN sit exactly halfway through the 26-letter alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a former student of a school or college, i.e. someone who was once a pupil there.

clue.text: Maxims useful to carpenters

explanation.surface: Wise sayings are handy for woodworkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb or saying; saws are also the toothed cutting tools a joiner uses.

clue.text: General 16 invading Italy

parts.note: 16 down is a mountaineer: the clue describes a famous military commander who crossed the Alps with elephants to attack Rome

explanation.surface: A military commander who climbed mountains to invade Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Carthaginian commander crossed the Alps in 218 BC to attack the Romans, making him a general who was a mountaineer of sorts.

clue.text: Welsh to avoid this colony

explanation.surface: Someone reneges so as to dodge paying up, in a new outpost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh' is not about Wales: to welsh is to dodge paying a debt, so a welsher avoids the paying-off of what is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement is both the paying of a debt (what a welsher avoids) and a newly founded community of colonists.

clue.text: To the French, notes suitable for dawn chorus

parts.note: au is French for 'to the'
B, A, D and E are four musical notes

explanation.surface: Suggests a French phrase about musical notes fit for birds singing at sunrise.
explanation.definitionFit: An aubade is a song or poem greeting the morning, a musical piece for daybreak.

clue.text: Australian bounder so sound a philosopher

indicators.note: the word is said out loud here, so a pair of words is pronounced to give the name

parts.note: a kangaroo is an Australian bounder, shortened to roo, followed by so

explanation.surface: A leaping Australian animal is so healthy that it is a great thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' first reads as 'healthy' but signals that ROO SO is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was the eighteenth-century Genevan thinker who wrote The Social Contract.

clue.text: Composer of sacred work (note catch)

parts.note: a mass is a sacred musical work
E is a musical note
to net a fish is to catch it

explanation.surface: A composer of church music, with a note about catching something.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Massenet was the French composer of operas such as Manon and Thaïs.

clue.text: Unfortunate pair embracing pair of batsmen

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it, as arms hold someone

parts.note: in cricket a batsman's pair is two ducks, two scores of nought, written as two zeros

explanation.surface: Two hapless cricketers in partnership at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'pair' in cricket is being out for nought (a duck) in both innings, so the pair of batsmen gives two O shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor can mean unlucky or deserving pity, as in 'the poor fellow'.

clue.text: Very old dismissed, ending military training

parts.note: passing is an old-fashioned word for very, as in 'passing strange'
a batsman dismissed is out

explanation.surface: A veteran is discharged at the end of army training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very old' looks like an elderly person, but it means 'very' in old usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A passing-out is the parade marking a cadet's graduation at the end of military instruction.

clue.text: Bold an' true characters assembled here

definitions.text: Bold an' true characters assembled here

indicators.note: the letters are gathered and put together in a fresh order

parts.note: a clipped spelling of and, giving the letters A and N

explanation.surface: Brave and honest heroes gathered at a famous meeting place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembled' rearranges BOLD, AN and TRUE; the knights who sat there were bold and true, so the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's knights met at a circular table so none would sit at its head.

clue.text: Leader of 10,000 in the theatre

explanation.surface: A commander of ten thousand men appears on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme's grand old duke had ten thousand men; the Duke of York's is also a West End theatre in London.

clue.text: Two-thirds of scales are a disgrace

annotationWithheld.why: Two-thirds of scales are a disgrace (7), SCANDAL: SCAL (two-thirds of SCALES) leaves NDA, which 'are a' does not give; no parse found and no source online
annotationWithheld.clue: Two-thirds of scales are a disgrace

clue.text: Find him in plain? It's unusual

definitions.text: Find him in plain? It's unusual

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters appear in an odd, rearranged order

explanation.surface: Coming across a mountaineer on flat ground would be strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges PLAIN and ITS; the whole clue also says a climber is rarely found on a plain.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpinist is a climber of high mountains, who would rarely be found on flat land.

clue.text: Colour of island revealed, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the words are pronounced rather than spelt

parts.note: Skye is a Scottish island, and to blew a secret (blew the gaff) is to reveal it

explanation.surface: The hue of a Scottish island is finally disclosed.
explanation.walkthrough: SKYE is an island in the Scottish Hebrides; 'revealed' gives BLEW, as in blew the gaff.
explanation.definitionFit: Sky blue is a pale shade of azure, the tint of a clear daytime heaven.

clue.text: Prohibit articles of woollen material

parts.note: to bar is to prohibit
a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article
a again, another indefinite article

explanation.surface: An instruction to ban items made of wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Barathea is a fine wool fabric with a broken rib weave, used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: Letters composed in support of board

indicators.note: composed, as a printer composes type, signals the letters set in a new order

explanation.surface: Correspondence written to back the board of directors.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a framework of legs on which a tabletop rests, a stand for a plank.

clue.text: Manager of company for one Paris-Rome trip

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a trip, as in tripping up, signals the letters stumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre manager takes the company on a tour from Paris to Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges I with PARIS and ROME.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario organises and finances concerts, operas or theatrical productions.

clue.text: Can it take a hundred abandoning vessel?

definitions.text: Can it take a hundred abandoning vessel?

indicators.note: the vessel word gives up the hundred, leaving the rest behind

parts.note: a craft is a boat or ship
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Asks whether a lifeboat can carry a hundred people leaving a sinking ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' takes C out of CRAFT; the whole clue also pictures crew abandoning ship onto one.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft is a flat floating platform, the thing evacuees might scramble onto when leaving a ship.

clue.text: Coarse cloth for decorating wall

explanation.surface: Rough fabric is used to decorate a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Frieze is a heavy woollen cloth with a napped surface; a frieze is also a decorated band along the top of a wall.

clue.text: Information to Welshman from European citizens

parts.note: gen is slang for information
Evans is a typically Welsh surname

explanation.surface: Information passed to a man from Wales by people from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Genevans are inhabitants of Geneva, a Swiss city.

clue.text: Horse mounted at first in 18

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the letters climb upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: the opening letters of 18 down, barathea

explanation.surface: A horse ridden at the start of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' turns BARA, the first four letters of 18 down's BARATHEA, upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arab is a breed of horse famed for speed and endurance.

clue.text: Drink knocked back — goes quickly in cups etc.

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is swallowed, but here the word is read backwards

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
to hie is to hasten, so hies means goes quickly

explanation.surface: A drink downed in one before hurrying off, in cups and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking but turns PORT into TROP.
explanation.definitionFit: Trophies are prizes such as cups, shields and plaques.

clue.text: Purse full pay all the contents to girl

indicators.note: the contents of each word are its inner letters, without the first and last

explanation.surface: A full purse; pay everything inside it to a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The insides of PURSE, FULL and PAY are URS, UL and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursula is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Wherewith to get power reduced in wave?

definitions.text: Wherewith to get power reduced in wave?

parts.words: Wherewith to get power reduced in wave?
parts.note: a harbour wall built to weaken the force of incoming sea surges

explanation.surface: Asks what weakens the strength of a wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakwater is a barrier out to sea that shelters a harbour by absorbing the energy of the waves.
